protocol: D-000 turn 2 of 3, same cycle as turn 1; refute not confirm; PREFERENCE-LADEN scoped D-006 fleet-class successor plus RULE-GOVERNED naming of the v3 reserved G03/G04 identifiers; not a fourth turn of CONTESTED D-101
summary: My one turn-1 finding landed, and it landed as an enforcing rule rather than a gesture. I re-measured rather than carrying my turn-1 numbers forward: built against MacOSX15.4.sdk on this host and ran all four call forms against a thin arm64 target. posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np with count=1, pref={CPU_TYPE_ARM64}, subpref={CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY} returns 0 with ocount=1 and the matching spawn succeeds; the same call with pref={CPU_TYPE_X86_64} also returns 0 with ocount=1 and the spawn then fails rc=86 EBADARCH, so the architecture request is genuinely enforcing in both directions. With subpref=NULL both directions return 22 EINVAL, leave ocount untouched, and the subsequent posix_spawn succeeds rc=0 completely unconstrained -- exactly the fail-open seam D102-T1-SF-1 described. Step 1's new clause rejects on a non-zero return or ocount != 1, which catches that path on the return code alone (and redundantly on ocount, which is never written on the EINVAL path), and the new Alternatives bullet records the measured behaviour accurately. Step 5's spawn conjunct is now backed by a checked call instead of an unchecked one. The turn-1-to-turn-2 diff is confined and I read every hunk: protocol header, disposition table, macOS preflight step 1, one Alternatives bullet, and the dispatch table's heading and three rows. Both numbered launch sequences are byte-identical, as are the path/digest identity bullets, the paired 10% formula, thin-only scope, preflight items 1-9, and the whole Linux target-process protocol. The attack list sweeps clean. Nothing hashes P between purge and cold -- sequence step 2 purges, step 3 is stat-only with an explicit 'no hash', step 4 is the cold exec. sysctl.proc_cputype appears three times and every one is a rejection citing D101-T1-MF-1. Weekly rolls explicitly do not suppress the 10% rule and are handled as paired strata. Warm p50 is telemetry that must not fail qualification, which matches D-006, whose clause 3 bounds only cold p50/p95/p99 and warm p95/p99. D-006's numerals are untouched: I read D-006 directly and the RSS bounds 40/50 and 60/100, the regress-only 10% rule from the second qualified release, the analyze and consented-probe exclusions, and the three original runner classes all match what the entry quotes and what its reversibility line restores. Nothing claims QUALIFIED, DEMONSTRATED, or SATISFIED; there is no implementation authorization and no condition-5 flip; ADV-D101-T3-01 is not reopened, and I checked its compressed disposition against both numbered sequences rather than taking the claim on trust -- inode-only stat after purge before the cold launch and before the unpurged doctor launch, no stat or hash inside the pair, which is what the sequences say. All seven cited digests re-measure byte-exact, the D-101 predecessor commit is HEAD, and the D-101 turn-3 subject and both its turn-3 reviews still measure to the values turn 1 cited, so no frozen subject moved between turns. I simulated all five file-08 edits in a scratch copy outside the repo: each anchor occurs exactly once, PARTLY MET, '16 of 18', 'D-006 machine pins owed' and 'D-006-conforming successor' all fall to zero, G03/G04 keep SPECIFIED/OPEN with no SATISFIED, condition 4 reads MET and condition 2 stays NOT MET. I checked the 18-of-18 arithmetic against the gate table itself rather than accepting it: 22 rows, 16 currently carrying a 'named: harness.*' prefix, and the D-088 denominator excludes G13, G06, G11 and G17, so naming G03 and G04 is exactly 18 of 18 and the only deficiency file 08 itself records for condition 4 is cleared. I have no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX.

notesList.title: Measurement scope: runtime is macOS 26.5.2 arm64; the Intel-host mirror of step 1 is not measurable here
notesList.detail: I record what I could and could not measure. API availability is verified directly against the SDK the entry names: /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX15.4.sdk exists on this host, posix_spawnattr_setarchpref_np is declared there at spawn.h:147 with the (attr, size_t, cpu_type_t*, cpu_subtype_t*, size_t*) signature the entry assumes, CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY is machine.h:145 ((cpu_subtype_t) -1), P_TRANSLATED is proc.h:178 0x00020000 exactly as the entry states, PROC_PIDARCHINFO and struct proc_archinfo are absent from the whole SDK include tree, proc_bsdinfo carries pbi_start_tvsec and pbi_start_tvusec with PROC_PIDTBSDINFO_SIZE = sizeof(struct proc_bsdinfo), and struct proc_bsdshortinfo has no start-time member of any kind. Every macOS API claim in the entry and in its Alternatives list is therefore confirmed against the named SDK. The runtime behaviour, though, was observed on this host: arm64, macOS 26.5.2, not a macos-15 fleet VM, and there is no Intel hardware here, so the macos-15-intel direction of step 1 is verified only as the API-level mirror (CPU_TYPE_X86_64 + CPU_SUBTYPE_ANY returns 0 with ocount=1 on this host too, and correctly refuses to spawn a thin arm64 image). The rule is symmetric and argument-level, so I see no residual risk, but the entry's contract is discharged on the fleet VMs, not here, and I am not claiming otherwise.

notesList.title: The disposition table dropped both prior-cycle MUST-FIX carry-forward rows; substance is preserved elsewhere in the file
notesList.detail: Turn 1's table carried three rows: ADV-D101-T3-01 accepted with its rule spelled out, plus 'remains accepted' rows for D101-T2-MF-1 / ADV-D101-T2-01 (no full-file hash between purge and cold) and D101-T1-MF-1 (ISA is the derivation, not sysctl.proc_cputype). Turn 2's table keeps ADV-D101-T3-01, adds the new D102-T1-SF-1, and substitutes D101-T2-SF-1 for both MUST-FIX rows, so the turn-2 ledger shows no MUST-FIX entry at all. I checked whether anything is actually lost from the file's bytes and it is not: D101-T2-MF-1 and ADV-D101-T2-01 are named in the path/digest identity heading and rejected by name in Alternatives ('Hash P between purge and cold exec'), and D101-T1-MF-1 is named both in the macOS protocol prose and in Alternatives ('Use sysctl.proc_cputype+PID as process arch'), each with the operative rule intact in the body. The table has been a rolling per-turn selection since turn 1, which itself omitted D101-T2-SF-1 and the whole D-099 series, and the prior-cycle dispositions live in D-101's own record. I also verified the two substituted-in claims rather than assuming them: 'split check on both platforms' matches preflight item 2 and the macOS path-identity paragraph, and 'disposition matches the numbered sequence' matches both numbered sequences bullet for bullet. Provenance is thinner between turns than it was, which is why I record it, but no rule weakened and no accepted finding was reopened, so this is not an objection.

notesList.title: The 18-of-18 denominator excludes G13, G06, G11 and G17; verified against the gate table, not assumed
notesList.detail: The whole decision turns on condition 4 flipping to MET, so I reconstructed the count from the register rather than trusting the entry. File 08 has 22 DR-G rows. Sixteen carry a 'named: harness.*' prefix (G01, G02, G05, G07, G08, G09, G10, G12, G14, G15, G16, G18, G19, G20, G21, G22). Six do not: G03, G04 and G13 are 'reserved, not named', G17 is 'dropped / inapplicable (D-077) ... not required-now', and G06 and G11 carry evidence prose with no identifier. D-088 -- ADOPTED at turn 1 with CONSENT from both reviewers -- set this denominator explicitly: sixteen recordable required identifiers written, G03/G04 and G13 reservation-only, G17 not required-now, G06/G11 unchanged, snapshot rewritten to 16 of 18, with the standing instruction not to present 16 of 16. The arithmetic only closes at 16 of 18 if G13 sits outside the required set alongside G06, G11 and G17, and file 08's own condition-4 cell confirms it by naming G03/G04 as the sole 'required and unnamed' pair. So naming G03 and G04 clears the only deficiency the register records, D-102 does not shrink the denominator to manufacture the result, and the entry's 'Does not name G13' is consistent rather than convenient. Worth stating plainly for the record: after this edit four of the twenty-two gate rows will still carry no named harness identifier while condition 4 reads MET. That is D-088's settled disposition, not D-102's act, and G13's OPEN status and reserved cell stay visible in the gate table, so I raise it as visibility rather than as a finding against this entry.
